studies.label: 24-week classroom intervention: ChatGPT-4-supported versus traditional music instruction
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No adjustment for class-level assignment is reported. MANCOVA and latent growth modeling are described at the participant level; class counts, class identifiers, class effects, and class-clustered standard errors are not provided (PDF pp. 5, 8-9, 12).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract (total sample and group allocation); PDF p. 12, Table 6, Creativity rows (analyzed arm counts)
counts_source.quote:
A quasi-experimental design was employed with 74 undergraduate music students assigned to an experimental group (n= 36) and a control group (n= 38).
Creativity Experimental 4.71 0.18 36
Control 4.35 0.17 38

arms.name: Experimental (ChatGPT-4 supported)
arms.description: Students used ChatGPT for musical ideas, guided prompts, feedback, correction, and revision during ordinary music coursework; they were encouraged to evaluate and adapt its output and submitted interaction screenshots or links (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 3.1-3.2 and 3.6; Table 1).

arms.name: Control (traditional instruction)
arms.description: Equivalent teacher-led coursework using lectures, handouts, textbooks, class notes, and teacher consultation, without AI; the same instructor taught both conditions (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.2 and Table 1).

studies.task: Second-year Bachelor of Music students produced compositions, improvisations, reharmonizations, stylistic adaptations, and arrangements with accompanying musical analyses during ordinary coursework (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 3.1-3.2 and 3.6; Table 1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 (identified as ChatGPT-4o in Section 3.1)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1: "the newer generation of ChatGPT-4 (i.e., ChatGPT-4o)"; PDF p. 4, Section 2.3, model announcement attributed to OpenAI (2024); PDF p. 18, References: "OpenAI. (2024). GPT-4o system card."

studies.shared_sample: Same cohort as Zhou and Kim (2024), Innovative music education: An empirical assessment of ChatGPT-4’s impact on student learning experiences. PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, says the students were drawn from that earlier cohort. The present intervention provides new data; earlier condition membership and its relation to the present class allocation are not stated.

estimates.outcome: Adjusted expert-rated creativity of musical products
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert ratings of musical products on four seven-point dimensions: originality of musical ideas, overall musical value, inventiveness in development, and expressive impact (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3). Two external music experts independently scored submissions, blinded to identity, condition, and submission timing; large rating discrepancies were discussed (PDF p. 7, Section 3.5). The aggregation of dimensions and raters is not specified.

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated. The paper labels this effect size η² and does not identify it as partial eta squared.

sources.quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed with 74 undergraduate music students assigned to an experimental group (n= 36) and a control group (n= 38).

estimates.notes: Adjusted marginal means and the Group univariate test following MANCOVA, controlling for prior ChatGPT use, Week 1 creativity, and Week 1 analytical skills (PDF p. 9, Results RQ2). The paper calls the Week 1 scores baseline and says baseline comparisons preceded intervention (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1); the exact assessment schedule relative to initial AI access remains unclear. The dependent variable's measurement occasion or aggregation is not stated. Arm counts are printed in Table 6; the total is the main-study sample printed in the abstract. Participant-level analysis is reported, with no class-level correction despite class-level assignment; se_basis does not establish valid precision for pooling. No mean difference or SD is computed from the reported numbers.

estimates.outcome: Linear growth slope of expert-rated musical creativity
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert ratings of musical products on four seven-point dimensions: originality of musical ideas, overall musical value, inventiveness in development, and expressive impact (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3). Two external music experts independently scored submissions, blinded to identity, condition, and submission timing; large rating discrepancies were discussed (PDF p. 7, Section 3.5). The aggregation of dimensions and raters is not specified. Linear latent growth model across repeated assessments; arm entries are latent mean slopes (PDF pp. 8-9, Results RQ1 and Table 3).

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 3, Creativity / Slope row (Experimental and Control: Est., Std. Err., p-value)

estimates.notes: The arm means and SEs here are the estimated means and SEs of the latent linear slope factors, not outcome levels at the final occasion or a treatment-indicator regression coefficient. The paper compares the slopes descriptively but prints no between-group slope difference, SE of that difference, or test. Table 3 prints within-arm p-values as < .000; these are not entered as a between-arm p-value. Model-specific analyzed participant counts are not stated, so all estimate-level counts are null. The growth models have participant-level random intercepts and slopes (PDF pp. 8-9, Results RQ1), but no class-level correction is reported. Repeated assessments occur during AI-supported coursework; no withdrawal outcome is measured. Calendar-week versus measurement-occasion scaling is unclear, so the slopes are preserved in the paper's units.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert ratings on a parallel seven-point rubric covering accuracy of harmonic and structural labelling, clarity of theoretical justification, depth of reasoning, and transferability of reasoning to novel contexts (PDF p. 7, Section 3.3). The same two blinded external assessors evaluated the submissions (PDF p. 7, Section 3.5). The aggregation of dimensions and raters is not specified.

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated. The paper labels this effect size η² and does not identify it as partial eta squared.

not_extracted.reason: Instrument calibration with twelve students outside the main sample; no randomized AI comparison and below the participant threshold (PDF p. 7, Section 3.4).

not_extracted.what: Initial creativity and analytical-thinking levels (latent intercepts)
not_extracted.reason: Initial-performance parameters, not post-intervention effects of the currently assigned assistance; no eligible post-baseline contrast is isolated by these parameters (PDF p. 8, Results RQ1; PDF p. 9, Table 3).

not_extracted.what: Latent intercept and slope variances and intercept-slope covariances
not_extracted.reason: Describe individual differences and associations between initial performance and growth within each arm, rather than an AI-versus-comparison outcome contrast (PDF pp. 8-9, Results RQ1).

Omnibus MANCOVA test across two distinct dependent variables, not a separate scalar output outcome. The outcome-specific Group tests and adjusted means are extracted separately (PDF p. 11, Table 4; PDF p. 12, Tables 5-6).

not_extracted.what: Prior ChatGPT use and baseline-score predictor tests
not_extracted.reason: Covariate associations do not estimate the randomized instructional-group contrast; the Group rows are retained (PDF p. 11, Table 4; PDF p. 12, Table 5).

not_extracted.what: Autoregressive paths, cross-lagged paths, and end-point creativity-analysis correlations
not_extracted.reason: Associations involving skills measured during the intervention and group comparisons of those associations, not total assignment effects on output levels. Cross-lagged paths condition on preceding skill outcomes (PDF pp. 8-10, Sections 3.7 and Results RQ3; PDF p. 12, Table 7).

not_extracted.what: Creative idea, creative revision, analytical check, and analytical structure co-occurrences and activation over time
not_extracted.reason: Epistemic network and activation analyses use only the experimental group; they supply no randomized AI-versus-comparison contrast on a scored output outcome (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.3 and 3.7; PDF p. 10, Results RQ4; PDF p. 14, Table 8).

not_extracted.what: Markov transition probabilities among creative and analytical moves
not_extracted.reason: Process analysis of experimental-group interaction sequences only, with no comparison arm (PDF p. 8, Section 3.7; PDF p. 11, Results RQ5; PDF pp. 15-16, Figures 5-6).

not_extracted.what: Separate rubric dimensions of creativity and analytical thinking
not_extracted.reason: The rubric dimensions are described but no dimension-specific arm means or group contrasts are reported. The reported overall creativity and analytical rubric scores are retained (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.3; PDF p. 12, Tables 5-6).

not_extracted.what: Individual-occasion creativity and analytical-thinking trajectory levels
not_extracted.reason: Individual-occasion trajectory levels are shown in figures, without a corresponding table of occasion-specific arm means. No values were read from the graphs; printed slope parameters are retained (PDF pp. 10-11, Figures 1-2; PDF p. 9, Table 3).

open_items: The number of randomized classes per arm and the allocation procedure are not stated (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1). The current codebook requires at least two classes per arm, so that requirement cannot be confirmed. The screening form's earlier statement that no minimum class count is required is superseded by the supplied codebook; extraction does not resolve this eligibility uncertainty.

No class-adjusted uncertainty is reported. The participant-level SEs and tests do not demonstrate appropriate precision for class randomization; class identifiers and class-level analysis would be needed before pooling (PDF pp. 5, 8-9, 12).

Participant-level arm SDs are not printed for either rubric outcome. Table 6 supplies adjusted mean SEs only; Table 3 supplies latent-parameter SEs. No SD or standardized mean difference has been derived.

The dependent variable time point or aggregation for MANCOVA is unspecified, and the mapping of Week 1 baseline scores to the claimed pre-intervention assessment is not explicit (PDF pp. 5-7, 9). If those covariates were measured after treatment began, the adjusted records would not meet the extraction rule.

Growth-model analyzed counts and the time coding of slopes are not explicitly stated. The paper describes biweekly submissions over a multi-semester intervention but labels trajectories by weeks; no time-unit conversion was made (PDF pp. 5, 7-10).

Aggregation across rubric dimensions, assessors, and repeated submissions is not specified. Output-rating reliability is not reported; the reliability for interaction-log coding is a different measure (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.3 and 3.5).
Earlier treatment membership and its relation to the current allocation are not given despite cohort overlap (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1).
The claimed baseline comparability tests refer to tables that contain instructional content and growth-model fit instead; initial-performance parameters differ by arm (PDF pp. 5-6, 9).
No posted data or supplement is identified; data are available on request from the corresponding author (PDF p. 17, Data availability).
notes: Extracted by A on 2026-10-10. The complete markdown was read from the title through the final reference; there are no appendices in the saved document. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf. PDF and printed page numbers agree. Table values were confirmed in PDF text; automatic table detection did not recover the main results tables. Quotes retain the printed numerical precision. No effect, SD, SE, p-value, confidence interval, or plotted point was computed. The paper calls the design quasi-experimental but explicitly reports class-level random assignment (PDF p. 5); class-count eligibility and class-adjusted precision remain unresolved. Total analyzed participants follows the stated main-study sample and the analyzed arm counts, with no reported attrition; no degrees of freedom were used to infer counts. Growth-model-specific counts are left null. Analytical rubric results extend the screening form's outcome map under the extraction instruction to retain output-scored outcomes and are coded other, never primary or pooled. All retained results concern work produced with AI available; withdrawal is proposed as future research (PDF p. 16, Section 5.3). No across-people similarity outcome is reported. The model year is supported by the paper's cited model announcement and system-card reference; an exact model snapshot is not specified.
